capability_summaries.name: Conditional Access
capability_summaries.plain_name: Smarter sign-in rules
capability_summaries.outcome: Decide who can sign in, from where, on which devices, and whether they must prove it is really them (for example with multi-factor authentication).
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Passwords alone are not enough. Good sign-in rules stop many everyday account takeovers before damage is done.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Your licenses include advanced sign-in rules, but they may still be loose or incomplete.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P2
capability_summaries.plain_name: Deep protection and visibility on PCs and devices
capability_summaries.outcome: See attacks on laptops and servers in more detail, find weak software, and respond before a single infected PC becomes a company-wide problem.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Devices are where people work. If they are not enrolled in advanced protection, you are flying partly blind.
capability_summaries.if_unused: You may be paying for advanced device protection on seats that are not fully enrolled.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Defender for Identity
capability_summaries.plain_name: Watchdogs on your on-site directory (if you still have one)
capability_summaries.outcome: Spot attackers moving through traditional office servers and Active Directory, not only cloud sign-ins.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Many organizations still rely on on-site domain controllers. Cloud-only tools cannot see every attack path there.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Identity threat sensors may be missing or unhealthy, so on-site directory attacks stay invisible.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 P1
capability_summaries.plain_name: Safe Attachments and Safe Links essentials
capability_summaries.outcome: Detonate risky attachments and rewrite dangerous links for licensed users even when the full P2 investigation pack is not present.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Many tenants own P1-level email protections that never leave default off states.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Safe content policies may be missing, scoped to pilots, or left in evaluation mode.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 P2
capability_summaries.plain_name: Stronger email and file threat protection
capability_summaries.outcome: Open risky attachments and links in a safe way, catch advanced phishing, and investigate email threats faster when something slips through.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Most business breaches still start with email. Better email protection reduces ransomware and invoice fraud.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Extra email protections in your license may still be off, in test mode, or only covering a few people.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Defender XDR
capability_summaries.plain_name: Cross-product incident correlation
capability_summaries.outcome: Connect identity, email, endpoint, and cloud signals into incidents that show the full attack story instead of isolated alerts.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Attackers hop products. Siloed alerts hide the path from phishing to privilege.
capability_summaries.if_unused: XDR correlation may be licensed while automated investigation and response stay idle.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Entra ID P2
capability_summaries.plain_name: Stronger control over admin accounts
capability_summaries.outcome: Give people powerful admin rights only when they need them, and get better tools to catch risky sign-ins on high-value accounts.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Admin accounts are the keys to your email, files, and business apps. If one is stolen, an attacker can look like a trusted employee.
capability_summaries.if_unused: You are paying for stronger admin protections that are not fully turned on yet.

capability_summaries.name: Exchange Online
capability_summaries.plain_name: Business email and calendar in the cloud
capability_summaries.outcome: Host mailboxes in Microsoft 365 and apply tenant email security and sharing controls that protect everyday business communication.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Email remains a primary business channel and a primary attack path. Weak tenant defaults leave phishing and data exposure wide open.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Mailboxes may be licensed while core protection and audit settings stay at weak defaults.

capability_summaries.name: Exchange Online Protection
capability_summaries.plain_name: Baseline spam and malware filtering for email
capability_summaries.outcome: Filter obvious junk and malware before it reaches inboxes, as the foundation under optional Defender for Office 365 controls.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Without baseline filtering, every advanced email control sits on a weak floor.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Core anti-spam or anti-malware policies may be off, overly permissive, or unmonitored.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Entra ID Protection
capability_summaries.plain_name: Alerts when a sign-in looks suspicious
capability_summaries.outcome: Automatically spot odd sign-in behavior (impossible travel, leaked passwords, unfamiliar locations) and require extra proof or block access.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Attackers often use valid passwords. Risk detection helps catch the session even when the password was correct.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Suspicious-sign-in protection is included in your plan but may not be enforcing anything yet.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Intune
capability_summaries.plain_name: Manage and protect company devices and apps
capability_summaries.outcome: Require healthy devices, push secure settings, and protect work data on phones and PCs people already use.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Unmanaged devices are a common path around strong cloud identity controls.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Compliance or configuration profiles may be missing, unassigned, or never enforced.

capability_summaries.name: Azure Log Analytics
capability_summaries.plain_name: The log store behind security analytics
capability_summaries.outcome: Land security and operational logs in a workspace that detections and investigations can query.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Sentinel without healthy log ingestion is an empty command center.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Workspaces may exist while critical tables are missing, short-retained, or never connected.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Sentinel
capability_summaries.plain_name: A central security command center in the cloud
capability_summaries.outcome: Bring security signals together in one place, detect patterns humans miss, and automate parts of incident response.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Without a place that correlates events, teams drown in alerts from many products and miss the story that ties them together.
capability_summaries.if_unused: A security workspace may exist, but few detections or smart analytics are turned on.

capability_summaries.name: OneDrive for Business
capability_summaries.plain_name: Personal work files in the cloud
capability_summaries.outcome: Give people a private work drive while still enforcing sharing limits, device access, and retention expectations.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Personal work drives often hold the same sensitive files as shared libraries.
capability_summaries.if_unused: OneDrive sharing or sync controls may lag behind the SharePoint tenant baseline.

capability_summaries.name: Power BI Pro
capability_summaries.plain_name: Shared interactive business reports
capability_summaries.outcome: Publish and share interactive reports with colleagues under tenant-level export, sharing, and guest boundaries.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: BI content often contains concentrated business truth; loose sharing leaks strategy.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Tenant sharing or export settings may still allow broader distribution than intended.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Power Platform
capability_summaries.plain_name: Low-code apps, flows, and environments
capability_summaries.outcome: Let teams build useful apps and automations inside governed environments with DLP and tenant isolation boundaries.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Ungoverned makers can connect business data to personal connectors overnight.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Environment creation, connector policies, or tenant isolation may still be wide open.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Purview Audit
capability_summaries.plain_name: A searchable record of important activity
capability_summaries.outcome: Reconstruct who did what across mail, files, and admin actions when something goes wrong.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Without audit history, investigations stall and compliance questions go unanswered.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Audit logging may be off, truncated, or never queried after an incident.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance
capability_summaries.plain_name: Oversight for risky business communications
capability_summaries.outcome: Detect harassment, threats, or sensitive-data sharing patterns in business conversations.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Toxic or noncompliant communication creates legal and cultural risk that identity tools miss.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Communication compliance may be entitled but never scoped to the channels that matter.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
capability_summaries.plain_name: Guardrails so sensitive data is harder to leak
capability_summaries.outcome: Warn or block people when they try to share credit cards, health data, or other sensitive information in the wrong place.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Accidental oversharing is common. Guardrails protect customers and reduce regulatory and reputational harm.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Data-protection rules may be missing or still in "test only" mode, so nothing is enforced yet.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery
capability_summaries.plain_name: Legal hold and investigation search
capability_summaries.outcome: Preserve and search relevant content when legal or investigative work demands it.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Missing holds destroy evidence and create legal and regulatory exposure.
capability_summaries.if_unused: eDiscovery tools may be licensed while no one can run a defensible case workflow.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
capability_summaries.plain_name: Early warning for risky insider activity
capability_summaries.outcome: Spot patterns that suggest data theft, leak, or policy abuse by people who already have access.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Trusted access is powerful. Without signals, insider incidents surface only after damage.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Insider risk policies may be unlicensed in practice or never moved past trial defaults.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management
capability_summaries.plain_name: Retention rules that keep or remove content on schedule
capability_summaries.outcome: Keep content for legal or regulatory periods and remove it when it is no longer needed, reducing both evidence risk and storage cost.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Retention protects evidence and reduces over-retention risk and storage cost.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Retention policies may be absent, so content is either deleted too early or kept indefinitely without a defensible schedule.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Purview Sensitivity Labels
capability_summaries.plain_name: Labels that classify and protect files and mail
capability_summaries.outcome: Mark sensitive content and apply encryption or access limits that travel with the file.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Classification without enforcement is a sticker; labels with protection change outcomes.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Labels may exist but remain unpublished, unused, or never auto-applied.

capability_summaries.name: SharePoint Online
capability_summaries.plain_name: Team sites and shared file libraries
capability_summaries.outcome: Host shared libraries with clear external sharing boundaries and default link permissions that match how the business actually works.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Over-broad sharing turns one mistaken link into a public data leak.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Tenant sharing defaults may still allow anyone links or unmanaged access.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Teams
capability_summaries.plain_name: Chat, meetings, and teamwork hub
capability_summaries.outcome: Keep collaboration fast while controlling guests, anonymous join, apps, and recording exposure.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Teams is where decisions and files move quickly — weak meeting or guest defaults become an easy side door.
capability_summaries.if_unused: External access, lobby, or app policies may still favor convenience over control.

findings.title: Phishing-resistant MFA not enforced for privileged roles
findings.summary: No enforced phishing-resistant MFA policy covers highly privileged roles.
findings.remediation: Target highly privileged directory roles with an enforced phishing-resistant MFA Conditional Access policy.
findings.customer_title: Require strong sign-in for powerful admin roles
findings.customer_summary: Admin accounts may still sign in with weaker multi-factor methods.
findings.customer_next_step: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for Global Administrator and other highly privileged roles.

findings.title: Intune licensed seats vs enrolled devices gap
findings.summary: Large Intune enrollment gap: 2 managed vs ~100 licensed units (2%).
findings.remediation: Enroll missing devices into Intune (Windows, iOS, Android, macOS); align license assignment with actual endpoints; investigate unmanaged devices.
findings.customer_title: Some paid device-management seats may not be enrolled
findings.customer_summary: You appear to pay for device management on many seats, but few devices are enrolled.
findings.customer_next_step: Compare Intune licenses to enrolled devices and enroll the missing ones through the device management tools you already use.

findings.title: Risky tenant-wide delegated app consent present
findings.summary: Found 1 tenant-wide delegated grant(s) with high-impact scopes.
findings.remediation: Audit oauth2PermissionGrants with AllPrincipals and high-impact scopes; remove unused grants.
findings.customer_title: Review apps with broad permissions for everyone
findings.customer_summary: Some apps have broad mail, files, or directory permissions for everyone.
findings.customer_next_step: Review and remove high-impact AllPrincipals OAuth grants that are not required.

findings.title: User consent to applications not restricted
findings.summary: User consent to applications is not tightly restricted.
findings.remediation: Configure authorization policy permission grant policies so users cannot consent broadly.
findings.customer_title: Stop users from approving risky app permissions
findings.customer_summary: Users can still approve app permissions themselves, which is a common path for consent phishing.
findings.customer_next_step: Restrict user consent so only admins approve non-trivial permissions.

findings.title: Weak authentication methods still enabled
findings.summary: Weak authentication methods remain enabled: sms.
findings.remediation: Disable SMS, Voice call, and Email OTP in Authentication methods policies.
findings.customer_title: Turn off SMS, voice, and email one-time codes
findings.customer_summary: SMS, voice, or email one-time codes are still allowed — these are the easiest multi-factor methods for attackers to abuse.
findings.customer_next_step: Disable SMS, Voice, and Email OTP authentication methods.

findings.title: Device code authentication flow not blocked
findings.summary: No enforced Conditional Access policy blocks device code flow.
findings.remediation: Create an enforced Conditional Access policy blocking authentication flow Device code flow for all users.
findings.customer_title: Block device-code phishing sign-ins
findings.customer_summary: Device-code phishing can still complete a successful sign-in.
findings.customer_next_step: Enforce a Conditional Access policy that blocks device code flow.

findings.title: High-risk sign-ins not blocked by Conditional Access
findings.summary: No enforced Conditional Access policy blocks high-risk sign-ins.
findings.remediation: Create an enforced Conditional Access policy blocking sign-in risk level High for all users.
findings.customer_title: Block suspicious high-risk sign-ins
findings.customer_summary: Suspicious high-risk sign-ins may still succeed.
findings.customer_next_step: Enforce a Conditional Access policy that blocks high sign-in risk.

findings.title: High-risk users not blocked by Conditional Access
findings.summary: No enforced Conditional Access policy blocks high-risk users.
findings.remediation: Create an enforced Conditional Access policy blocking user risk level High for all users.
findings.customer_title: Block accounts Microsoft marks as high risk
findings.customer_summary: Compromised accounts marked high risk may still sign in successfully.
findings.customer_next_step: Enforce a Conditional Access policy that blocks high user risk for all users.

findings.title: Legacy authentication not blocked by Conditional Access
findings.summary: No enforced Conditional Access policy blocks legacy authentication.
findings.remediation: Enable an all-user Conditional Access policy that blocks Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy clients.
findings.customer_title: Block outdated sign-in methods
findings.customer_summary: Outdated sign-in methods may still work without multi-factor checks.
findings.customer_next_step: Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks legacy authentication for all users, with documented emergency-access exclusions only.

findings.title: Phishing-resistant MFA not enforced for all users
findings.summary: No enforced all-user phishing-resistant MFA policy was found.
findings.remediation: Create a Conditional Access policy requiring the Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength for all users.
findings.customer_title: Require strong phishing-resistant sign-in for everyone
findings.customer_summary: Users can still sign in with weaker multi-factor methods that phishing can defeat.
findings.customer_next_step: Enforce phishing-resistant authentication strength for all users where feasible.

findings.title: No alert on Global Administrator activation
findings.summary: No notification rule found for Global Administrator activation.
findings.remediation: Configure PIM notifications for Global Administrator activation.
findings.customer_title: Alert when Global Admin is turned on
findings.customer_summary: Global Admin can be activated without a clear alert path.
findings.customer_next_step: Enable notifications for Global Administrator activation.

findings.title: Global Administrator activation does not require approval
findings.summary: Global Administrator activation does not require approval.
findings.remediation: Configure PIM role settings so Global Administrator activation requires approval.
findings.customer_title: Require approval to turn on Global Admin
findings.customer_summary: Someone eligible for Global Admin can turn it on without a second approver.
findings.customer_next_step: Require approval on Global Administrator PIM activation.

findings.title: Privileged provisioning appears outside PIM
findings.summary: Highly privileged roles are assigned permanently with no PIM eligibility schedules — provisioning appears outside a PAM workflow.
findings.remediation: Require PIM eligibility for highly privileged roles and remove standing bypass paths.
findings.customer_title: Provision admin access only through just-in-time tools
findings.customer_summary: Powerful admin access is granted permanently without a just-in-time system.
findings.customer_next_step: Stop direct permanent privileged assignments and route access through PIM.

findings.title: Permanent highly privileged role assignments present
findings.summary: Found 2 permanent highly privileged role assignment(s).
findings.remediation: Remove standing highly privileged assignments and prefer eligible PIM activation.
findings.customer_title: Remove always-on powerful admin assignments
findings.customer_summary: Some powerful admin roles are permanently on instead of just-in-time.
findings.customer_next_step: Convert highly privileged standing assignments to PIM-eligible where possible.

findings.title: PIM licensed but privileged access not operationalized
findings.summary: Found 4 standing privileged role assignment(s) and 0 PIM eligible schedules — just-in-time admin access is not in use.
findings.remediation: Convert standing admin roles to PIM-eligible where possible, require activation with MFA/justification, and review permanent role assignments.
findings.customer_title: Admin accounts still have "always on" superpowers
findings.customer_summary: Admin superpowers appear permanently on. Time-limited admin access (included in your stronger identity plan) does not look like it is being used.
findings.customer_next_step: Ask IT to turn on time-limited admin access for your top admins first (Global Administrator and similar roles).

findings.title: Security defaults enabled instead of Conditional Access
findings.summary: Security defaults are enabled, providing baseline MFA protections and blocking legacy authentication. Licensed Conditional Access customization remains unused.
findings.remediation: Create equivalent Conditional Access policies for MFA and legacy-authentication blocking in report-only mode, with appropriate emergency-access exclusions. Validate their coverage and sign-in impact. Only then disable Security Defaults and immediately enable the validated policies in a controlled cutover.
findings.customer_title: Move from Security Defaults to customizable sign-in rules
findings.customer_summary: Security Defaults already includes baseline MFA protection and blocks outdated sign-in methods. Your plan also includes smarter sign-in rules you can customize, but that paid capability remains unused.
findings.customer_next_step: Create equivalent Conditional Access policies for MFA and legacy-authentication blocking in report-only mode. Validate coverage, exclusions, emergency access, and sign-in impact; then perform a controlled cutover from Security Defaults to the validated policies.

findings.title: Defender for Endpoint licensed seats vs onboarded devices gap
findings.summary: Large Defender for Endpoint onboarding gap: 40 onboarded vs ~100 licensed units (40%).
findings.remediation: Onboard missing devices via Intune, GPO, or scripts; investigate unhealthy sensors; align license assignment with actual endpoints.
findings.customer_title: Some PCs may not be enrolled in advanced device protection
findings.customer_summary: You appear to pay for advanced device protection on many seats, but relatively few devices are enrolled.
findings.customer_next_step: Compare licensed seats to enrolled devices and enroll the missing ones (often through your device management tools).

findings.title: DLP does not cover key locations
findings.summary: No DLP policy workload locations could be determined.
findings.remediation: Enable DLP for Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, and devices where licensed.
findings.customer_title: Apply DLP across Exchange SharePoint OneDrive Teams
findings.customer_summary: We could not find DLP policies covering your data locations.
findings.customer_next_step: Enable DLP for Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, and devices where licensed.
limitations: Per-location coverage is derived from policy workload flags, not a full location enumeration.

findings.title: Sensitivity labels are not auto-applied
findings.summary: No auto-labeling policy is configured.
findings.remediation: Configure auto-labeling (default labels or auto-labeling policies) so that sensitive content is classified automatically and consistently.
findings.customer_title: Turn on auto-labeling for sensitive content
findings.customer_summary: Content must be labeled by hand. Configure auto-labeling so sensitive content is classified consistently.
findings.customer_next_step: Configure auto-labeling policies or default labels so new and existing content is classified automatically, then monitor the results.

findings.title: Access Reviews licensed but not configured
findings.summary: No access review definitions were found. Access Reviews are included in the tenant's plan but have never been configured.
findings.remediation: Create access review definitions for privileged directory roles and guest user access; configure recurring cadence and reviewers.
findings.customer_title: Set up periodic access reviews for admins and guests
findings.customer_summary: Your plan can periodically confirm who still needs powerful access and clean up old guest accounts. That process does not look set up yet.
findings.customer_next_step: Create an Access Review for your Global Administrators and guest users (monthly or quarterly), then review the first round of results.

findings.title: Risky AI agents not clearly blocked
findings.summary: No Conditional Access policy clearly blocks risky AI agents.
findings.remediation: Configure available Conditional Access or identity protection controls that block risky AI agents.
findings.customer_title: Block risky AI agents when the control is available
findings.customer_summary: We did not find an automated block for risky AI agents. Confirm in Entra whether agent risk controls are available and enforced for your tenant.
findings.customer_next_step: Review Entra AI agent risk controls and enforce blocks where licensed and supported.
limitations: AI agent risk controls vary by cloud and license; treat this as advisory.

findings.title: Admin consent workflow not enabled
findings.summary: Admin consent request workflow is not enabled.
findings.remediation: Enable admin consent requests and assign reviewers who monitor the queue.
findings.customer_title: Turn on admin approval requests for apps
findings.customer_summary: There is no structured way for users to request admin approval for apps.
findings.customer_next_step: Enable the admin consent request workflow with monitored reviewers.

findings.title: Application credentials expired or expiring soon
findings.summary: Found 0 credential(s) expiring within 30 days and 1 already expired.
findings.remediation: Rotate expiring credentials and monitor end dates for all app registrations.
findings.customer_title: Rotate expiring app secrets and certificates
findings.customer_summary: Some app secrets or certificates are expired or about to expire.
findings.customer_next_step: Rotate credentials expiring within 30 days and remove already-expired secrets.

findings.title: Application password addition not blocked
findings.summary: No enforced policy blocking application password addition was found.
findings.remediation: Block app password creation via Conditional Access or disable legacy per-app passwords.
findings.customer_title: Block legacy app passwords
findings.customer_summary: Users may still create app passwords that skip modern multi-factor checks.
findings.customer_next_step: Block creation of app passwords with Conditional Access or authentication method controls.

findings.title: Non-admin users can register applications
findings.summary: Non-admin users can register applications.
findings.remediation: Set Users can register applications to No in Entra user settings / authorization policy.
findings.customer_title: Stop regular users from creating apps
findings.customer_summary: Anyone in the directory can create app registrations, which expands the attack surface for malicious apps.
findings.customer_next_step: Disable user application registration in Entra user settings.

findings.title: Authenticator login context not fully enabled
findings.summary: Microsoft Authenticator is enabled without full login context (app_name=False, location=False).
findings.remediation: Enable display of application name and geographic location for Microsoft Authenticator push notifications.
findings.customer_title: Show app and location on Authenticator prompts
findings.customer_summary: Authenticator prompts do not clearly show app and location context, which makes push phishing harder to spot.
findings.customer_next_step: Enable application name and geographic location in Microsoft Authenticator notifications.

findings.title: Managed devices not required by Conditional Access
findings.summary: No enforced managed-device Conditional Access policy was found.
findings.remediation: Create an enforced Conditional Access policy requiring compliant or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices.
findings.customer_title: Require company-managed devices for access
findings.customer_summary: Users may access work apps from unmanaged personal devices.
findings.customer_next_step: Enforce Conditional Access requiring compliant or hybrid-joined devices.

findings.title: MFA registration not limited to managed devices
findings.summary: No enforced policy requires a managed device for MFA registration.
findings.remediation: Create an enforced Conditional Access policy targeting user action Register security information with managed device grants.
findings.customer_title: Only allow multi-factor setup from managed devices
findings.customer_summary: Attackers with a stolen password may register their own multi-factor method.
findings.customer_next_step: Require a managed device when users register security information.

findings.title: Dormant privileged identities still enabled
findings.summary: Found 2 enabled privileged principal(s) with no successful sign-in or workload activity in the last 90 days (2 user(s), 0 workload identities of 4 privileged principal(s)).
findings.remediation: Disable or archive unused privileged accounts, remove unneeded role assignments, and prefer just-in-time access via PIM.
findings.customer_title: Powerful accounts that nobody uses are still switched on
findings.customer_summary: Some powerful accounts are still switched on but have not been used recently. Unused admin accounts and workload identities are a favorite target for attackers.
findings.customer_next_step: Review enabled admin accounts that have not signed in for a long time; disable or remove access you no longer need.

findings.title: Guest directory access not limited
findings.summary: Guest users have the same directory permissions as members.
findings.remediation: Set guestUserRoleId to Guest User or Restricted Guest in authorization policy.
findings.customer_title: Limit what guests can see in your directory
findings.customer_summary: Guest accounts can see directory information similar to full members.
findings.customer_next_step: Set guest user access to limited or restricted in Entra external collaboration settings.

findings.title: Guest invitations not limited to inviter roles
findings.summary: Guest invitations are broadly allowed (allowInvitesFrom=everyone).
findings.remediation: Set allowInvitesFrom to adminsAndGuestInviters (or stricter).
findings.customer_title: Stop everyone from inviting external guests
findings.customer_summary: Many users can invite external guests without a special role.
findings.customer_next_step: Allow only admins and Guest Inviter role holders to invite guests.

findings.title: No alert on highly privileged role assignment
findings.summary: No PIM notification rules were found for privileged role assignments.
findings.remediation: Configure PIM notification rules for privileged role assignment events.
findings.customer_title: Alert when powerful roles are assigned
findings.customer_summary: Powerful role assignments may happen without an alert.
findings.customer_next_step: Enable PIM notifications for privileged role assignment events.

findings.title: Purview DLP licensed but not enforced in production
findings.summary: Secure Score suggests DLP is largely unused (2 controls, ~10% completion).

evidence.note: Uses Microsoft Secure Score DLP/information-protection controls as a proxy when direct Purview policy APIs are unavailable to the app.

findings.remediation: Deploy core DLP policies for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and endpoints; move from simulation to enforce after tuning.
findings.customer_title: Guardrails against accidental data leaks may not be active
findings.customer_summary: You appear to pay for data-leak protection that is not meaningfully enforced yet. Confirm in the Purview portal.
findings.customer_next_step: Start with a simple policy for email and cloud files that detects obvious sensitive data, then move from "test" to "enforce" after a short tuning period.
limitations: Secure Score proxy — verify DLP enforce mode in Purview portal.
Based on Microsoft Secure Score signals — confirm the real setting in the Microsoft 365 / security admin portal before treating this as definitive.

findings.title: Sentinel automation rules / playbooks not configured
findings.summary: No Sentinel automation rules or playbooks were found.
findings.remediation: Configure automation rules that trigger playbooks for high-value alerts and confirm at least one runbook-style playbook is enabled.
findings.customer_title: Automate part of the incident response
findings.customer_summary: Your security workspace reacts to nothing automatically — every alert waits for a person.
findings.customer_next_step: Add automation rules that trigger playbooks for common alerts, so response starts without waiting for a person.
